newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Soymeal price outlook constructive - Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Soymeal price outlook constructive - Oil World.

text.p: A slowdown in U.S. soymeal crushings in the past two weeks has exacerbated tight supplies, giving a constructive price outlook for the next two to four months, Hamburg-based Oil World said.

Supplies were already squeezed by acute old crop tightness and delays to new crop harvesting, with mill stocks dropping faster than expected to 192,000 tonnes at the start of September, the newsletter said.

"Unless a surprise occurs in the form of a significant upward revision of U.S. soybean supplies and a corresponding sizeable decline in soybean prices (which we do not expect at the moment) soyameal is likely to trend higher," it added.

The newsletter also cited strong demand from the emerging markets of Asia, seasonally increasing meal requirements in the northern hemisphere countries in the upcoming winter and a shortfall in Argentine and Brazilian exports.
These are expected to decline by one million tonnes, or 12 percent, in the Oct/March 1996/97 period from a year earlier.
Soybean values will also be supported by the decline in world production and supply of other oilseeds.
Despite a 400,000-tonne upward revision in the Chinese rapeseed crop this week, global production is expected to drop by 4.3 million tonnes, or 12 percent, in 1996/97, Oil World said.
